advances: Refutes deletion of full-body equality from the proper varying-fraction positive cap-cover setting, without a critical-cap conclusion.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
In cyclic order take
$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,2),(-2,-1),(2,-3),(2,-1)\},\\
B&=\operatorname{conv}\{(-13/8,17/8),(-5/2,-1/2),(3/2,-5/2),(3/2,-1)\}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The common edge inequalities in order have left sides $-3x+y,-x-2y,x,x+y$ and right sides $(5,4,2,1)$ for $A$, $(7,7/2,3/2,1/2)$ for $B$. Their right-side averages bound the Minkowski midpoint. The resulting polygon $K$ has vertices $(-21/16,33/16),(-9/4,-3/4),(7/4,-11/4),(7/4,-1)$, each the average of the corresponding endpoint vertices. This gives the reverse containment. The origin strictly satisfies all four inequalities in all three bodies. The cuts $H_1=\{x\ge0\}$, $H_2=\{y\ge0\}$ and $H_3=\{x+y\le0\}$ are therefore proper and their three normals sum to zero, span the plane and have no positively dependent pair.

Write $A_i=A\cap H_i$ and likewise $B_i,K_i$. The maps $T_i(p)=\lambda_i p+v_i$ with $(\lambda_i,v_i)$ respectively $(3/4,(0,-1/4)),(17/16,(-9/16,0)),(1,(-1/2,1/2))$ send $A_i$ onto $B_i$. The averaged map $(\operatorname{Id}+T_i)/2$ sends $A_i$ onto $K_i$. To check the first cut, on $A_1$ the bounds are $0\le x\le2$ and $-2-x/2\le y\le1-x$. The two affine substitutions give the corresponding bounds with upper $x$ values $3/2,7/4$, lower intercepts $-7/4,-15/8$ and upper intercepts $1/2,3/4$. These are exactly the bounds of the respective clipped polygons. On $A_2$ the bounds are $y\ge0$ and $(y-5)/3\le x\le1-y$. The maps give the left bounds $(y-7)/3,(y-6)/3$ and right bounds $1/2-y,3/4-y$, respectively. On the third cut the $x+y$ upper bound of each polygon is redundant, and translation by $v_3$ or $v_3/2$ preserves the cut and shifts the other three inequalities to the correct right sides. Convexity of $A_i$ now gives $K_i=(A_i+B_i)/2$ and homothety gives cap-area root equality.

Shoelace area for the whole polygons and direct integration of the clipped polygons give
$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
& A&B&K\\\hline
\text{whole}&10&271/32&1183/128\\
H_1&5&45/16&245/64\\
H_2&8/3&289/96&363/128\\
H_3&55/8&55/8&55/8
\end{array}
$$
For example, the first two $A$ caps integrate widths $3-x/2$ over $[0,2]$ and $8/3-4y/3$ over $[0,2]$, respectively, with the first width computed from its displayed bounds. For $A_3$, the clipping vertices are $(-2,-1),(2,-3),(2,-2),(-5/4,5/4)$ and give area $55/8$. The affine maps give the $B,K$ columns of the cap rows by their squared ratios. The normalized endpoint pairs are $(1/2,90/271),(4/15,289/813),(11/16,220/271)$, all unequal. The lower sloping edge of $A,B$ has common vector $(4,-2)$ and the right vertical edges have vectors $(0,2)$ and $(0,3/2)$, so no positive global homothety exists. The quantities $4|K|-|A|-|B|=37/2>0$ and $(4|K|-|A|-|B|)^2-4|A||B|=7/2>0$ give strict whole-body Brunn–Minkowski.

Place $A,B$ at bases $-1,1$. Their hull has exact middle section $K$ and no other integer bases. Its mass is the sum of the whole areas in the table. The largest area is $10$ and is less than half this mass. The ambient cuts are the pullbacks of $H_i$ and their mixed masses are unequal by the cap table.
statement: There are full-dimensional planar convex bodies $A,B,K=(A+B)/2$ and three proper halfspaces through a common interior point of all three bodies, with normals forming a full-rank minimal positive circuit, such that each cap satisfies captured-side Brunn–Minkowski equality and has unequal normalized endpoint fractions. The endpoints are nonhomothetic quadrilaterals with strict whole-body Brunn–Minkowski inequality. At bases $-1,0,1$ these bodies are actual fibers of one complete convex mixed family of mass $3547/128$ with largest fiber area $10<3547/256$.
title: A proper planar positive cap circuit need not glue cap homotheties
